disease_label_per_paper: Suspected intentional potassium cyanide poisoning (up to 5 g ingested) with complete recovery despite delayed hydroxocobalamin
presentation_summary: 25-year-old woman with a mood disorder (venlafaxine, mirtazapine, lamotrigine) found unconscious at home; an empty package labeled 5 g potassium cyanide and a suicide note lay next to her; several antidepressant tablets were missing; last contact about 2 h 45 min before she was found; admitted to the Toxicology Unit roughly 1 h later.

On admission: GCS 6, inadequate shallow irregular spontaneous respiration, trismus, SpO2 ~92%, BP 75/45 mmHg, HR 120/min, pupils initially dilated then mid-sized with anisocoria R>L, cool moist skin with preserved pink coloration; no bitter almond odor detected.
ABG: pH 7.004, HCO3 8.2 mmol/L, PCO2 34.6 mmHg, PO2 80.7 mmHg, lactate 22.0 mmol/L, base excess -23.0 mmol/L.

Labs: WBC 28.62 x10^3/uL, Hb 13.4 g/dL, platelets 331 x10^3/uL, urea 41.5 mg/dL, creatinine 1.72 mg/dL, Na 142.7, K 4.26 mmol/L, Mg 3.27 mg/dL, Ca 2.40 mmol/L, AST 52, ALT 18 IU/L, PT 12.9 s, INR 1.16, CK 384 U/L, CRP 34.1 mg/L, glucose 97 mg/dL.
Head CT (hospital day 1) without acute abnormality; initial chest radiograph with normal aeration, no edema or focal inflammatory change.

risk_context.source_text_value: An empty package labeled as containing 5 g of potassium cyanide and a suicide note were found next to the patient. As the product was not analytically verified and the exact amount ingested could not be independently confirmed, the exposure was considered a suspected ingestion of up to 5 g of potassium cyanide.
risk_context.note: Scene/history evidence available at presentation; not analytically verified.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Blood thiocyanate 0.66 mg/dL on admission (colorimetric; lab thresholds toxic >15, lethal >20 mg/dL); blood cyanide not measured
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Toxicological testing performed on admission demonstrated thiocyanate in the blood at a concentration of 0.66 mg/dL. ... Direct measurement of blood cyanide concentration was not performed

confirmatory_findings.finding: Blood ethanol not detected (0.00 g/L); antidepressant/lamotrigine levels not assessed
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Ethanol was not detected. Venlafaxine, mirtazapine, lamotrigine, and their metabolites were not specifically assessed

confirmatory_findings.finding: Diagnosis based on circumstances of exposure and clinical presentation
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Given the high clinical suspicion of cyanide poisoning based on the circumstances of exposure and the clinical presentation, treatment decisions were based primarily on clinical findings

clinical_course_events.finding: Hemodialysis then hydroxocobalamin 5 g IV ~4 h after admission; acidosis resolved (lactate 2.0 mmol/L) within 9-14 h; later suspected aspiration pneumonia; extubated day 7
clinical_course_events.source_text_value: Hydroxocobalamin was administered at a dose of 5 g intravenously over 15 minutes. ... Metabolic acidosis resolved, and the lactate concentration decreased to 2.0 mmol/L.

actual_treatment: intubation and mechanical ventilation with 100% oxygen
intravenous fluids, norepinephrine, sodium bicarbonate, sedation
ceftriaxone and amikacin for suspected aspiration pneumonia

outcome.source_text_value: Complete Recovery Following Intentional Potassium Cyanide Poisoning Despite Delayed Hydroxocobalamin Administration

quality_warnings: The exposure history (empty potassium cyanide package, suicide note) is presentation-time scene evidence and is kept rankable; ingestion was not analytically verified.
Blood thiocyanate, blood ethanol and other toxicology results are kept non-ranking.
Temperature and respiratory rate were not reported at admission.
Urea (mg/dL) converted to BUN (x28/60); total calcium mmol/L converted to mg/dL (x4.008).
Head CT was performed during hospital day 1 (after intubation); structured as presentation imaging.
